text:
Alex Formenton's return to the NHL with Edmonton has drawn criticism. He was one of five members of Canada's 2018 world junior team found not guilty of sexual assault in 2025, and the Edmonton Journal reported this week that a victims' rights group is screening a documentary in the city in response to the signing.

On the ice, he's playing 12 minutes a night on the fourth line, with two goals and five points in 25 games and nothing in his last 12. Edmonton gets 34% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, 15 points worse than without him. The Oilers have also scored 8.4 more goals than the chances deserve with him on, so his on-ice results are flattered.

NHL Edge has him among the fastest skaters in the league, 98th percentile in top speed and acceleration. That's what earned him the contract after his time in Switzerland with Ambri-Piotta.

What to watch: whether the speed turns into chances. His minutes have dropped to under 11 lately, which suggests the coaching staff is still deciding.
